label: Next Senate Majority Leader: Schumer Vs. Van Hollen
kicker: The Race For Senate Democratic Leader
title: Chuck Schumer Vs. Chris Van Hollen
why: Senate Democrats choose their leader in December. Chuck Schumer has led them since 2017. On November 12, Chris Van Hollen announced he is running against him. Here is how the two have voted:

groups.name: Blocking Arms Sales To Israel
groups.about: Six attempts to stop specific sales of bombs, rifles and bulldozers. All failed.
groups.more: Congress can block an arms sale to another country by passing a resolution against it. Senators forced votes on six of these, each covering a different sale to Israel. Four covered bombs or bomb guidance kits, one covered rifles for Israel's national police, and one covered Caterpillar bulldozers. Every vote was on whether to pull the resolution out of committee, and every one failed, so none moved forward.

groups.name: The 2026 Defense Policy Bill
groups.about: Covers troop levels, weapons buying and military construction.
groups.more: This yearly bill sets policy for the military: how many troops, which aircraft, ships and missiles to buy, and construction on bases. It also covers military pay and health care. It sets spending limits but does not itself provide the money. The six votes were steps along the way, from starting debate to approving the final version. The first three were on the Senate's own version (S. 2296). The last three were on the final version agreed with the House, which traveled under a different bill number (S. 1071).

groups.name: Overturning An IRS Reporting Rule For Crypto
groups.about: Cancels a rule making some crypto platforms report sales to the IRS.
groups.more: In December 2024 the IRS issued a rule requiring decentralized finance platforms to report their customers' digital asset sales. Congress can cancel a recent rule by passing a resolution. The Senate voted on two versions of that resolution, each with one vote to take it up and one to pass it.

groups.name: Permanently Banning Fentanyl-Related Drugs
groups.about: Permanently puts fentanyl-related substances in the strictest drug category.
groups.more: The HALT Fentanyl Act permanently places fentanyl-related substances, as a class, in Schedule I, the strictest category of controlled drugs. Offenses carry the same penalties as other fentanyl analogues, including mandatory minimum prison terms. It also changes the rules for researchers who study these drugs.

groups.name: Advancing The Energy Permitting Bill
groups.about: Would change permit rules for energy projects. No final vote yet.
groups.more: The Senate is using a House tax bill, the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act (H.R. 2347), to carry a much larger package called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The package would set deadlines for federal permits and environmental reviews, set a 150-day limit for filing many lawsuits against them, and change rules for power lines, geothermal, hydropower, nuclear licensing, and mining. It would also change permit rules under the Clean Water Act and the Endangered Species Act. The text the Senate is debating (Senate Amendment 6883, offered November 10, 2026) keeps the original tax bill as its last part. That part would stop taxing most payouts won by survivors of sexual abuse. Two of these votes were on taking up the bill and one was on ending debate on the package. The Senate has not held a final vote on it.

groups.name: Taking Up The College Sports Bill
groups.about: Votes to start debate on rules for college sports. Both later voted against it.
groups.more: Both votes were on whether to start debate on the Protect College Sports Act. When the Senate passed the bill on September 28, 2026, 77 to 22, both senators voted no. As introduced, the bill sets national rules for athletes' name, image and likeness deals, caps agents' fees on those deals at 5 percent, and gives athletes one transfer without losing eligibility. It also lets schools and conferences pool and sell media rights, and keeps the cap on sharing revenue with athletes in place after a court settlement ends.

groups.name: Taking Up The Housing Bill
groups.about: Votes to start debate on a wide housing bill. Both later voted to pass it.
groups.more: Both votes were on whether to start debate on a housing bill the House had passed, the Housing for the 21st Century Act (H.R. 6644). The Senate then replaced its text with its own version, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, and passed it 89 to 10 on March 12, 2026. Both senators voted yes then, and yes again on the final version on June 22, 2026. The final version has 59 sections. Most create or change federal housing programs: support for permitting new kinds of apartment buildings, lighter environmental review for some rural projects, rules for manufactured housing, and closer oversight of housing counseling groups. It also has sections on community banks, limits on large investors buying single-family homes, and a bar, through 2030, on the Federal Reserve issuing its own digital currency.

groups.name: Luke Lindberg For A Top Agriculture Job
groups.about: Nominee for the Agriculture Department's top trade post.
groups.more: Nominated to be Under Secretary of Agriculture for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs. One vote ended debate on the nomination and the other confirmed him, 78 to 17.

groups.name: The 2026 Government Funding Bill
groups.about: Funds the military, health, education, transportation, housing and more.
groups.more: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 combines 5 of the 12 yearly funding bills. It funds the military and the Labor, Health, Education, Transportation, Housing, Treasury and State departments for the rest of the 2026 budget year, and Homeland Security through February 13, 2026.

groups.name: Advancing The March 2025 Stopgap Funding Bill
groups.about: Let a bill funding the government reach a final vote. Both then voted no.
groups.more: A continuing resolution that funded the government through September 30, 2025, the rest of that budget year, and avoided a shutdown on March 14, 2025. This was the vote to end debate on it, which needed 60 senators. Later the same day both senators voted against passing the bill itself, which passed 54 to 46.

groups.name: Sean Duffy For Transportation Secretary
groups.about: Nominee to run the Department of Transportation.
groups.more: Nominated to be Secretary of Transportation. The Senate confirmed him 77 to 22.

groups.name: Cutting The Defense Budget By 10 Percent
groups.about: Would have moved the money to veterans' dental care. Failed, 10 to 88.
groups.more: An amendment to the defense policy bill. It would have cut the amount the bill allows for the Pentagon by 10 percent, not counting military pay and the military health program, and used the money to expand dental care for veterans. It needed 60 votes and failed, 10 to 88.

groups.name: Setting Aside A Hemp Change In A Funding Bill
groups.about: Set aside an attempt to drop a new definition of hemp from the bill.
groups.more: The bill that ended the government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025 also changed the legal definition of hemp. An amendment tried to take that change out. The Senate voted 76 to 24 to set the amendment aside, which kept the change in the bill.

groups.name: Changing Debt Limit Instructions In The Budget
groups.about: A proposed change to the 2025 budget plan. Failed, 5 to 94.
groups.more: An amendment to the 2025 budget plan. The plan told Congress to raise the debt limit by $4 trillion in the House's instructions and by up to $5 trillion in the Senate's. The amendment would have changed both to $500 billion. It failed, 5 to 94.
